newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan parties seek stock option system by Mar 98.
newsitem.headline: Japan parties seek stock option system by Mar 98.

text.p: A panel from Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) and its allies will urge the government to allow all companies to introduce employee stock options by March 1998, party sources said on Thursday.
Under the panel's draft plan, all Japanese companies would be able to introduce stock options and issue warrants, the sources told Reuters.
A stock option system enables company executives and employees to buy shares in their own company at specified prices as incentives.
The system is popular in the United States and Europe but it is only allowed to venture capital companies in Japan under the nation's commercial code.
Japanese business leaders have said that the system would be effective in motivating employees to work hard.

The panel has decided to submit a bill to revise the commercial code by the end of this month to pave the way for the full liberalisation of the stock option system, the sources said. The bill is likely to pass in parliament during the current parliamentary session due to end in June, they said.
The bill is also aimed at easing regulations on share buy-backs by companies.
